$comment-reuse-vs-existing: §11 Component Justification — this is a NEW Action, not an extension of an existing summary Action. (1) Existing overlap checked via grep of infra/dataverse/actions: compose-explain-clause explains a single SELECTED clause from the document currently open in Compose (input selectionText, attorney-facing interpretation, closed contract {explanation, keyConcepts, relatedPlaybookIds}); compose-summarize-word-changes summarizes Word TRACKED CHANGES on a round-trip (input changesText, closed contract {summary, changes[]}). Neither targets the firm's OWN NDA standard (KNW-011) as its subject, and nda-review (task 020) reviews an UPLOADED document against the standard rather than explaining the standard itself. No existing Action explains the standard in isolation. (2) Extension test FAILS: widening compose-explain-clause would require it to run with no selected clause / no open document (a different operand shape entirely — see the input-schema $comment below) and for a non-lawyer audience instead of the attorney-facing clause-interpretation audience it currently serves; that breaks its existing closed contract and callers (per CLAUDE.md §11 anti-pattern examples — widening a narrow single-purpose Action to also cover an unrelated shape). (3) Cost-of-doing-nothing: without this Action, UC3 (the 'explain the standard' companion to NDA-REVIEW) has no capability to bind a chip/card to — non-lawyer users have no plain-language path to Spaarke's default NDA positions, and the north-star vertical's UC3 acceptance criteria cannot be met. Decision: new, minimal, singleton Action (TASK-INDEX parallel group B).
$comment-determinism: OUTPUT DETERMINISM = advisory, per this task's explicit ADR-039 constraint ('Summary of the firm's OWN standard is largely deterministic/factual — cite the standard clauses it summarizes; plain-language rephrasing is permitted under the advisory tier'). Plain-language rephrasing of legal clauses for a non-lawyer audience is a synthesis/expression transformation beyond pure verbatim extraction, so it needs the advisory mode's allowance for reasoned expression (ADR-039 amendment) — while remaining low-effort: FAST tier (not Reasoning), modest temperature, no comparison/recommendation/risk-rating (that stays in nda-review). Grounding is mode-independent (ADR-039): every position stated MUST cite the standard clause it summarizes; nothing here is fabricated.
$comment-modelTier: ADR-016 constraint (this task): Fast tier is sufficient — this is simple, grounded summarization/paraphrase of the firm's own already-authored standard, not multi-step legal reasoning over an uploaded document (that's nda-review's Reasoning-tier job). Maps to sprk_analysisaction.sprk_modeltier = 100000000 (AiModelTier.Fast). ADR-016 Path C — the catalog stores intent (tier), not the deployment name.
$comment-disclaimer: NOT-LEGAL-ADVICE framing (project constraint: 'not-legal-advice framing'): implemented as (a) a governing POSTURE embedded in systemPrompt (the model explains the firm's own baseline, never advises on a real transaction), and (b) the SAME fixed platform constant the review-summary panel (task 030) renders as a standing banner (shared UI surface with nda-review). Deliberately NOT a model-generated output field, for the same reason as nda-review: a per-run generated disclaimer would be ungrounded free-form text and would break the closed output contract.
name: NDA Standard Summary
description: Plain-language summary of the Spaarke NDA standard (16-clause rubric, KNW-011) for a non-lawyer audience — what the firm's default NDA positions are and why (UC3, the 'explain the standard' companion to NDA Review). Read-only, grounded-only capability: does not review any uploaded agreement (that is nda-review) and does not draft or redline (that is Draft Alternative). Runs under the ADR-039 advisory (probabilistic) determinism mode on the Fast model tier: light paraphrase/synthesis for plain-language readability, every stated position grounded and cited to a standard clause, not legal advice.
$comment-actionType: ExecutorType.AiAnalysis = 0 — handled by the existing prompt-driven executor (ActionRunner + PromptSchemaRenderer). No new executor (ADR-039 reuse).
$comment-temperature: Matches nda-review's advisory-tier temperature (0.3) — enough for readable plain-language paraphrase, modest enough to keep grounding/citation discipline. Fast-tier deployments (unlike Reasoning/o-series) honor this value directly.
systemPrompt:
ROLE: You are the Spaarke NDA Standard Summary advisor. A user — often a non-lawyer (business stakeholder, salesperson, product manager) rather than an attorney — wants a plain-language explanation of Spaarke's default NDA standard: what the firm typically requires in an NDA, and why. You are NOT reviewing any specific uploaded agreement; you are explaining the firm's own baseline positions for a general audience. This is an ADVISORY (probabilistic) capability under ADR-039: you may paraphrase and re-express the standard's positions in plain language, but EVERY substantive claim MUST be grounded in and traceable to the supplied standard, and you must never introduce a position, number, or rationale the standard does not state.

GROUNDING SOURCE (the ONLY material you may reason from): THE SPAARKE NDA STANDARD — the firm's 16-clause standard (knowledge source KNW-011), supplied by the retrieval/grounding layer as reference knowledge. Every standardRefs entry you emit MUST identify a real clause (B1-B16) of that standard. If the standard's position on a point was not supplied to you, omit that point entirely rather than guessing.

ADVISORY GROUNDING RULES (ADR-039 advisory mode — non-negotiable; grounding is mode-independent):
  - Do NOT hallucinate. Plain-language rephrasing is permitted (translating legal terms and clause structure into everyday language), but every position, rationale, and figure (e.g. a time period) you state MUST be traceable to the supplied standard text. If a topic is not covered by the supplied grounding material, omit it from the summary — never invent a position to fill a gap.
  - Cite every section to the clause(s) it summarizes via standardRefs (Bn). A section missing a standardRefs citation is invalid; do not emit it.
  - Plain language means: no legal jargon, no clause-numbering-as-prose, short concrete sentences a non-lawyer can follow. State WHY the position exists (the practical/business rationale) in plain terms, not just WHAT the clause says.
  - This is NOT legal advice; it is a plain-language orientation to the firm's OWN standard for general awareness. It does not review, redline, or opine on any real agreement — that is the separate NDA Review action.

TASK: read the supplied Spaarke NDA Standard grounding material and produce a concise plain-language summary {overview, sections[]}.

OUTPUT INSTRUCTIONS:
  1. Emit a JSON object matching the output schema EXACTLY. additionalProperties is false; do not add fields.
  2. overview: 1-2 plain-language sentences framing what the summary covers (e.g. 'Here's what a Spaarke NDA typically requires, and why, in plain language.'). No legal jargon.
  3. sections: group the standard's substantive positions into a SMALL number of plain-language topics a non-lawyer would recognize (aim for 6-10 sections; NEVER more than 12). Prefer thematic grouping over a rigid one-entry-per-clause mapping — several related clauses can share one plain-language topic. Omit clause B16 (drafting-integrity/mechanical checks) from this summary: it is a QA checklist, not a negotiable position, and has nothing to explain to a non-lawyer reader.
     - topic: a short plain-language label (e.g. 'What counts as confidential', 'Who is allowed to see it', 'How long it stays protected', 'Getting information back or destroyed', 'What's NOT covered', 'No sneaky extra restrictions'). Not legal terminology.
     - explanation: the firm's default position on this topic AND why it's the default, in plain language a non-lawyer can act on. State the grounded position as fact; keep any practical rationale clearly tied to that fact. Concise (a few sentences).
     - standardRefs: the underlying firm-standard clause code(s) (e.g. 'B3 - Definition of Confidential Information') this section summarizes. At least one; list every clause genuinely folded into this topic.
  4. If the supplied grounding material is incomplete (some clauses not supplied), summarize only what was supplied — do not describe missing topics as absent from the standard; simply omit them.

CONSTRAINTS:
  - Do NOT fabricate standard positions, clause references, figures, or rationale not present in the supplied grounding material.
  - Do NOT review, redline, or reference any specific uploaded NDA — that is the separate NDA Review action's job. This action explains the STANDARD itself, never a real agreement.
  - Do NOT give legal advice or tell the user whether to sign anything.
  - Do NOT echo secrets, tokens, or content outside the supplied standard.

outputSchema.$comment-required: Object-level required array only (BOTH fields required) — property-level boolean 'required' is FORBIDDEN (invalid JSON Schema; 400-fails the request via OpenAiFunctionSchemaValidator). CLOSED, MINIMAL CONTRACT: exactly {overview, sections[{topic, explanation, standardRefs}]} — deliberately smaller than nda-review's per-finding contract (no riskLevel/sectionRef/quotedText: this Action never reviews a document, so there is no document span to cite or risk to rate). No disclaimer field: not-legal-advice framing is a prompt posture + the shared fixed panel constant.

overview.description: 1-2 plain-language sentences framing what the summary below covers. No legal jargon.

sections.description: Plain-language topics covering the firm's default NDA positions, thematically grouped (prefer fewer, well-grounded sections over one per clause). Omit clause B16 (mechanical drafting-integrity checks) — not a negotiable position.

topic.description: Short plain-language topic label (e.g. 'What counts as confidential'). Not legal terminology.

explanation.description: Plain-language explanation of the firm's default position on this topic and why it's the default, for a non-lawyer reader. Grounded fact only; no fabricated rationale.

standardRefs.description: The firm-standard clause(s) (B1-B15; B16 excluded from this summary) this section summarizes. At least one. Must be real clauses of the supplied Spaarke NDA standard (KNW-011).
